channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Meets with Qarmet Steel Plant Employees
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev visited Temirtau and met with employees and trade union members of the Qarmet joint-stock company. He highlighted the region's rapid economic development, noting a significant increase in non-raw material exports and a substantial output in heavy industry. The President emphasized Qarmet's crucial role in the nation's industrial potential and the region's economy.

item.title: Kazakhstan Detains Ten Suspects in Alleged Plot to Overthrow Government
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Security Committee has detained ten individuals in Atyrau for allegedly plotting to forcibly change the constitutional order. The suspects are also accused of operating three underground educational centers for children and teenagers. Authorities seized firearms, drugs, and extremist materials during searches of the suspects' homes.

item.title: Afghan Students Recount Hope and Disbelief During Taliban Takeover
item.description: University students in Afghanistan describe their journey from hope to shock as provincial capitals fell to the Taliban. Despite approaching graduation, they believed security forces would prevail, never imagining the rapid collapse that led to widespread darkness and surrender orders.

item.title: Kazakhstan and China Establish Joint Investment Fund Up to $200 Million for TMTM
item.description: Kazakhstan and China are creating a joint investment fund, initially valued up to $200 million with potential for growth, to develop the Trans-Caspian International Transport Route (TMTM). Minister Serik Zhumangarin proposed defining responsible financial institutions to expedite its launch.

item.title: Man Arrested in Aktobe for Assaulting Doctor at Children's Hospital
item.description: A criminal case has been initiated against a father who assaulted a doctor at the Aktobe Regional Children's Hospital's reception department. The suspect was detained and placed in a temporary detention center. The incident occurred on October 31st after the father was dissatisfied with the medical assistance provided.

item.title: Afghanistan Tackles Substandard Fuel Imports Amid Quality Concerns
item.description: Afghanistan is facing challenges with the import of substandard fuel. The country is actively working to address the issue of poor-quality fuel entering its markets. This initiative aims to improve the quality of fuel available to consumers and ensure compliance with standards.

item.title: Kazakhstan May Introduce Special License Plates for Trucks Over 25 Tons
item.description: Kazakhstan is considering special license plates for trucks weighing 25 tons or more. This proposal aims to enhance control over heavy vehicles and regulate their movement on public roads, as current traffic intensity causes significant road damage. Specific implementation details remain unclarified.

item.title: Almaty Police Dismantle Synthetic Drug Laboratory in Residential Complex
item.description: Almaty police have dismantled a mini-laboratory producing synthetic drugs, specifically mephedrone, within a multi-story residential building. The 34-year-old suspect operated the lab on the top floor to avoid detection by neighbors. Authorities seized 4.5 kilograms of drugs and various production equipment. The suspect faces up to life imprisonment.

item.title: Kazakhstan and China to Establish Direct Investment Fund Up to $200 Million
item.description: Kazakhstan and China are working on establishing a joint direct investment fund, initially valued at up to $200 million with potential for future increases. This initiative, discussed during the Second Tien Shan Forum, aims to support the Trans-Caspian International Transport Route. Both countries are identifying financial institutions to define the fund's operational framework.

item.title: Russia and Azerbaijan Sign Deal for Armored Vehicle Repair Facility Modernization
item.description: Russia and Azerbaijan have signed an agreement to modernize and construct facilities for repairing armored vehicles used by the Azerbaijani military. The deal, announced November 1, follows the Organization of Turkic States summit. Russia may also supply Pantsir-S1 air defense systems.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Considers Stricter Radiation Control at State Borders
item.description: A proposal has been made to tighten radiation control measures at Kyrgyzstan's state borders. The initiative aims to enhance safety and monitoring of radioactive materials entering the country. Further details on the implementation and scope of these proposed controls are expected.

item.title: 22 Gas Filling Stations in Nukus Fined for Simultaneous Price Increases
item.description: Twenty-two gas filling stations in Nukus, Karakalpakstan, have been fined for colluding to raise compressed gas prices. The Committee for the Development of Competition investigated after a citizen complaint, finding prices increased by an average of 1050 UZS per cubic meter. Nine stations appealed the decision in court.

item.title: President orders investigation into eviction of disabled vendors in Talas
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov has ordered an investigation after disabled vendors in Talas were allegedly evicted from their market stalls. A 70-year-old woman reported that seven entrepreneurs, including those with disabilities, lost their trading spots on May 1, 2023, when their goods were removed and replaced with new vendors. Efforts to reclaim the spots have been unsuccessful.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Azerbaijan Expand Transport Cooperation with New Projects
item.description: Kazakhstan's Samruk-Kazyna and Azerbaijan's AZCON Holding have agreed to collaborate on a new Trans-Caspian ferry system, "Caspian Bridge." They also plan to establish an intermodal freight terminal and a joint venture. The agreements aim to boost container and cargo transportation along the Trans-Caspian International Transport Route.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Government Debt Servicing Costs to Rise Significantly by 2028
item.description: Kazakhstan's budget expenditures for servicing government debt are projected to reach 3.68 trillion tenge by 2028. Officials attribute this rise to an increasing budget deficit, the need for new borrowing, and changes in capital markets. Internal borrowing through government securities remains the primary source for deficit financing.

item.title: BMB Agro to Double Cotton and Grain Cultivation Areas Next Season
item.description: BMB Agro LLC in Arnasay district plans to double its cotton and grain cultivation areas next season. The company is currently undertaking agro-technical measures and has fulfilled its current year's grain and cotton cultivation plan. They aim to increase agricultural production by expanding cultivated land and improving land use efficiency.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Raise Mobile Transfer Tax Control Limit
item.description: Kazakhstan is set to increase the tax control limit for mobile transfers from 1.02 million to 1.557 million tenge within three months. The new regulations will calculate the limit based on the monthly calculated indicator (MCI), setting it at 360 MCI, which amounts to 1,557,000 tenge this year. Banks will report data to tax authorities if specific conditions are met over three consecutive months.

item.title: Uzbekistan's 'Second Chance' Project Shows Early Success in Inmate Rehabilitation
item.description: Uzbekistan's national 'Second Chance' project, initiated by the head of state, is yielding initial results in changing inmates' lives. Participants have achieved an average of 89% proficiency in English and 80% have successfully completed computer literacy courses, demonstrating the project's practical effectiveness.

item.title: Uzbekistan Explains Drinking Water Tariff Differences Across Regions
item.description: Uzbekistan's 'Uzsuvta'minot' joint-stock company has clarified the reasons behind varying drinking water tariffs across regions. Factors such as distance from water sources, pipeline maintenance, and pumping station operations contribute to the cost. For instance, a cubic meter of water costs 1400 soms for the public in Tashkent but 6800 soms in Surkhandarya region.

item.title: CEOs Identify Cybersecurity as Top Business Growth Risk, Increase Investment
item.description: Chief Executive Officers perceive cybersecurity as the primary risk to business growth and are consequently increasing their investments in cyber threat protection. This trend highlights the growing importance of digital security for corporate success.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Criticizes City Leaders for Embezzling Funds
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's President Sadyr Japarov stated that 200-300 million soms allocated for the development of Tokmok and Kara-Balta cities were misappropriated. He reminded local leaders of their personal responsibility for state finances, noting that some officials falsely reported completed work to pocket funds. Japarov emphasized that budget funds must be used for their intended purpose.

item.title: Kazakhstan Explores Reducing Dependence on Russian Oil Export Routes Amidst Risks
item.description: Kazakhstan, heavily reliant on the Caspian Pipeline Consortium (CPC) for oil exports through Russia, faces risks due to repeated disruptions. While alternative Caspian Sea shipments are growing, they remain limited. Challenges include falling water levels and higher transport costs, alongside geopolitical tensions. The country's export decisions impact regional energy infrastructure and trade.

item.title: Uzbekistan Proposes 100 Joint Projects for Turkic States
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev proposed a "Turkic World – 100" program for 100 joint investment and industrial projects among Organization of Turkic States (OTS) members. The initiative aims to boost industrial cooperation, focusing on rare minerals, renewable energy equipment, and value-added goods, financed via the Turkic Investment Fund.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Tree Planting Initiative Hampered by Wildfires and Low Seedling Survival
item.description: Kazakhstan is undertaking a massive tree planting project, aiming to plant two billion trees by 2027. However, the initiative faces significant challenges, including devastating wildfires like the one in Semey Ormany nature reserve and consistently low survival rates for planted seedlings, raising concerns about the program's effectiveness and long-term success.

item.title: German Court Rules Blocking of Alisher Usmanov's Lawsuit Against EU Council Illegal
item.description: A German court has declared the blocking of Alisher Usmanov's lawsuit against the EU Council illegal. The court ordered documents to be sent to the defendant in Belgium, overturning a previous decision by the presiding judge of the Hamburg Regional Court, which had refused to send them based on objections from the German Foreign Ministry.

item.title: Tajikistan and China Discuss Establishing Joint Ventures in Free Economic Zones
item.description: Tajikistan's Minister of Economic Development and Trade met with China Pingmei Shenma Holding Group Co., Ltd. to discuss cooperation. Both sides expressed readiness to establish joint ventures in Tajikistan, particularly within its free economic zones, building on high-level relations between the two countries.

item.title: Kazakhstan Road Sector Faces Over 8 Billion Tenge in Violations, 33 Investigations Launched
item.description: Over 8 billion tenge in damages have been identified in Kazakhstan's road sector, leading to 33 pre-trial investigations. Significant savings of 36 billion tenge were achieved by canceling unjustified tenders. Systemic violations were found in planning, construction, and operation phases, prompting calls for updated norms and new technologies.

item.title: Man Alleges Threats and Pressure from Kyrgyzstan's GKNB to President Japarov
item.description: During a meeting in Talas, a man named Meder told President Sadyr Japarov that GKNB (State Committee for National Security) officers allegedly threatened him and forced him to transfer property in August 2023. He claims they threatened imprisonment and seized his assets. A criminal case has been initiated against GKNB officers.

item.title: Google Pay Launches in Uzbekistan Following Data Protection Reforms
item.description: Google Pay has launched in Uzbekistan, enabled by recent changes to personal data protection rules. A senior Google executive stated that a more flexible approach to data storage, allowing processing abroad under certain conditions, facilitated the launch. Biometric and genetic data, along with telecom customer data, must still be stored domestically.

item.title: Excessive Taxes and Low Purchasing Power Cause Business Slump in Afghanistan
item.description: Medium-scale businesses in Afghanistan are facing a slump due to heavy taxes, numerous fees, and a sharp decline in purchasing power. Traders report daily revocation of business licenses and forced sales or closures. The Taliban collect money under various headings, including income tax and license renewal fees, making it difficult for businesses to cover costs and leading to capital loss.

item.title: Turkmenistan Cracks Down on Nas Sales, Causing Widespread Shortages
item.description: Turkmen authorities have initiated a crackdown on the sale of 'nas', a form of smokeless tobacco, leading to arrests and significant shortages. Residents report that nas vendors are closing shops, forcing consumers to travel to rural areas to find the product. This follows a similar, unexplained shortage of cigarettes last month.

item.title: Afghan Families Fleeing Taliban Education Bans Face School Rejection in Iran
item.description: Afghan families who relocated to Iran to continue their daughters' education after the Taliban's ban are facing new restrictions. Iran now requires residency documents or an Iranian parent for enrollment, while simultaneously refusing visa extensions. This leaves children in limbo, prompting calls for Iran to facilitate their access to education.

item.title: Uzbek President Calls for Prioritizing Locals for New Jobs
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev emphasized the need to regulate the employment of foreign citizens residing in Uzbekistan. He noted that the country is becoming more attractive to foreigners, with their numbers nearing 250,000. Mirziyoyev stressed that while maintaining openness, order is essential, urging authorities to track foreign residents' activities and income sources.

item.title: UN-Habitat Provides Solar-Powered Water Access to Over 100 Families in Herat
item.description: UN-Habitat reports that over 100 families in Herat's Zinda Jan district now have access to drinking water via a new solar-powered system. Previously facing difficulties, these families benefited from the project supported by the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA). This initiative addresses Afghanistan's ongoing water crisis.

item.title: Kazakhstan Military Deficiencies Found After 14 Servicemembers Died in Caspian Sea Incident
item.description: A comprehensive review of Kazakhstan's Ministry of Defense following the deaths of 14 military personnel during Caspian Sea exercises revealed shortcomings in risk assessment, safety oversight, and operational decision-making. Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov stated that measures are being implemented to enhance military safety, including the use of drones for surveillance and personal tracking devices.

item.title: Tajikistan President Inaugurates Juice Factory and New School in Devashtich District
item.description: Tajikistan's President Emomali Rahmon inaugurated a fruit and vegetable processing plant producing juices, LLC "Vitaminkhoi Tojikiston," and a new school in the Devashtich district. The factory, built by entrepreneur Saidmurod Davlatov, uses modern German and Italian equipment capable of processing 7,200 tons of produce annually and producing 2,700 liters of juice per hour.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Prosecutor General's Office Holds Meeting on Business Support and Rights Protection
item.description: Uzbekistan's Prosecutor General's Office convened a meeting focused on supporting entrepreneurship and protecting business rights. The meeting emphasized the importance of comprehensive support for businesses and improving the business climate, in line with President Shavkat Mirziyoyev's reforms. Since the beginning of the year, prosecutors have assisted over 21,500 entrepreneurs.

item.title: Uzbekistan's initiatives boost cooperation among Turkic states, says official
item.description: Uzbekistan's participation in the Organization of Turkic States (OTS) is enhancing economic ties, with trade volume increasing significantly since 2017. Official Bakhtiyor Mustafayev highlighted that initiatives proposed by Uzbekistan at the recent Ankara summit aim to address growing needs for joint production, financing, and streamlined procedures, fostering closer collaboration.

item.title: Kyrgyz President orders review of case involving men detained after dispute with prosecutor
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov has instructed the Deputy Prosecutor General to review the case of three men detained following a road dispute with a prosecutor. A woman claimed her husband and relatives were unjustly held after the incident, prompting the president to question the prosecutor's conduct and consider the detainees' release if no injuries occurred.

item.title: Uzbekistan Aims to Recognize Work Experience for Migrant Pensions Abroad
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to expand international cooperation to ensure migrant workers' service records and pension rights are recognized abroad. President Mirziyoyev stressed the need for this, noting citizens pay pension contributions in over 40 countries. Agreements are sought with Russia, Germany, Japan, and others.
